model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.eps_note: Statutory EPS is diluted by IAS 40 investment-property revaluations and one-off significant items (e.g., FY22 Retirement Living divestment gains, FY26 +202m fair-value uplift); FFO per security is the cleaner distributable-earnings series and is what this model discounts.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Reported OCF-based FCF is not used for CAGR purposes: it swings from -424m (FY24) to +654m (FY26) purely on MPC/LLC land-inventory timing, not underlying earnings power. FFO (the flow this model capitalises) is used instead.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FFO-per-security 9-year CAGR (1.1%), corroborated by the 3-year (-0.2%, MPC-cycle trough-to-peak noise) and 5-year (2.2%, COVID-adjacent) figures bracketing it. FY27 guided step to 38.0-39.0c is treated as a one-year mix-shift bridge (ex-MPC growth offsetting a fading MPC peak), not a new run rate -- terminal growth is capped at 2.5% (revenue basis), close to but slightly above the historical per-security trend to allow for the maturing capital-partnering fee-income and Data Centres platforms.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_note: Equity (book value) CAGR (0.85-2.25%) tracks FFO CAGR (1.19-2.51%) closely -- no >30% divergence. Unlike a passive landlord REIT where book value is pure IAS 40 cap-rate noise, Stockland's equity growth is a reasonable cross-check here because a meaningful share of FFO is retained (payout ratio 60-80%) rather than distributed, so equity partly reflects compounding retained development earnings alongside revaluations.
historical_growth.nta_cross_check: NTA/security was $4.22 at FY2025 and $4.25 at H1 FY2026 (KPI series); FY2026 year-end book equity/share (10,710/2,424.4 = $4.42) is a close proxy for FY2026 NTA. Current price $4.02 sits at an ~9-10% discount to book, consistent with a diversified group carrying above-average cyclical (residential) risk relative to passive-landlord REIT peers that often trade closer to or above NTA.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 lands on the guidance midpoint (38.5c FFO/security), then growth fades as the guided MPC settlement step-down works through before recovering to a 2% steady state on Logistics/Data Centres/fee-income maturation; FFO margin drifts to 24.5%; AFFO after a 7%-of-revenue capex charge capitalised at 9% cost of equity with a 17x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: FY27 beats the top of guidance as LLC, Logistics and Data Centres outperform and capital-partnering fee income keeps compounding at 20%+, lifting the FFO margin toward 27% while the capex charge falls as more growth is co-funded; 3% terminal growth, 19x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2H FY26's buyer-sentiment moderation deepens into a two-year MPC/LLC downturn, Workplace occupancy keeps sliding, cost of debt keeps rising toward 5.9%+ and gearing drifts toward the top of the target band, compressing the FFO margin to 21% and raising the capex charge to 9%; 1.5% terminal growth, 12x exit at a 9.5% cost of equity.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Stockland is valued as a stream of distributable earnings (FFO, the Group's own post-interest, post-tax capitalisation-basis measure combining Investment Management rental/fee income and Development profit), not as a pure operating-company owner-FCF DCF and not split into a sum-of-parts, because Stockland's own guidance and distribution policy is set off the single blended FFO number and a clean segment-level cash-flow split is not disclosed. FFO is capitalised at a 9.0% AUD cost of equity (above the ~8.5% used for passive-landlord AU REIT peers, reflecting Stockland's much higher exposure to the residential development cycle) with no debt deduction, since FFO is already struck after financing cost. The FY2027 guidance year (38.0-39.0c FFO/security) is anchored at its midpoint; thereafter growth fades toward the historical 9-year FFO-per-security trend of ~1.1%/yr, well below the guided one-off step, because management's own commentary frames FY27 growth as offsetting a fading MPC peak rather than a new run rate. The key judgment is the AFFO capex charge: sized to the Investment Management portfolio's disclosed recurring growth capex (~6% of revenue) rather than the much larger gross development spend, because MPC/LLC land and construction costs are already expensed against development revenue inside the FFO calculation -- charging them again as capex would double-count.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: each 50bp on the 9.0% moves the base value by roughly 8-10%; the sensitivity grid is the honest range.

MPC cycle depth and duration: FY27 guidance already prices in a step-down from the FY26 settlement peak (8,902 lots to 7,300-8,300); the bear case models a further two-year deterioration consistent with the 2H FY26 sentiment moderation management itself flagged.

Capex/AFFO definition: whether the Investment Management-only growth capex (~6% of revenue, used here) or a broader all-in figure including a slice of net land-bank investment (which would push the charge toward 9-10%, closer to SCG/GPT's convention) is the right AFFO deduction is a real modelling choice worth ~10-15% of value.

Rising cost of debt (5.3% FY26 to ~5.9% guided FY27, fixed-hedge ratio down from 76% to 65%) squeezes the FFO margin directly and, via mortgage-rate pass-through, MPC/LLC buyer affordability simultaneously -- a genuine double exposure the bear case captures in both the margin path and the discount rate.

Execution risk on unproven new platforms (Data Centres/EdgeConneX, expanded Commercial Development, further capital partnerships) sits in the FY27+ margin and growth paths but has essentially no track record to anchor it to.

Distribution payout was recalibrated from a tighter historical band to 60-80% of FFO in FY26 specifically to fund growth reinvestment; a resumption of the suspended DRP, or a widening of the payout range downward, would change dilution/retained-capital assumptions not modelled here.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.71-6.75.
data_sources.financials: SGP.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis tables (FY2015-FY2026, H1 FY2016-FY2026); FY2026 Annual Report FFO/PreTaxFFO/FFOPerShare KPIs, cash flow statement (payments for land/investment properties/plant/investments, lines 6584-6616), WANOS note (line 7223), issued capital note (line 9471), gearing/distribution-policy disclosure (lines 355-806, 7267), DRP note (lines 9487-9496).
data_sources.qualitative: SGP.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): FY26 results (FFO $892m +10.4%, FFO/security 36.9c top-end of guidance, gearing 22.7%, DRP suspended 2H26), FY27 guidance (FFO/security 38.0-39.0c, distribution flat 25.2cps, MPC 7,300-8,300 lots, LLC 850-950 sites, cost of debt ~5.9%), Data Centres/EdgeConneX partnership, capital-partnering platform (M&G/Invesco/Mercer/MSREI), bull/bear case axes.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 statutory revenue (Metrics.csv / core_metrics). FFO margin path is struck on this base: FY26 FFO 892 / 3589 = 24.85%.
inputs.share_count_basis: WANOS used in calculating diluted EPS, FY2026: 2,425,500,202 (FY2026 Annual Report note 7223). Issued capital at 30 June 2026 was 2,424,131,049 (note 9471). Held flat: FFO/DPS guidance is per security and the DRP (which added ~62-173m securities in some prior years) was suspended for 2H26 and its FY27 status is not yet disclosed; a resumed DRP would be modest annual dilution (<1%/yr historically) funding the capex already charged in the flows, not incremental to it.
inputs.net_debt_note: HELD AT ZERO BY DESIGN. FFO is Stockland's own capitalisation-basis measure, struck after net interest, tax and NCI (FY26 cash tax was actually a $11m benefit; effective tax rate disclosed at 20-30% across periods). Capitalising a post-financing-cost flow at the cost of equity and then deducting debt would charge the debt twice (SCG.AX/GPT.AX/CHC.AX/GMG.AX convention for AU stapled REITs/property groups). Actual 30 June 2026: borrowings ~4,895m (current 324 + non-current 4,571), gearing 22.7% (look-through 24.4%), within the 20-30% target band; A3/stable Moody's rating; H1 FY2026 gearing was 28.1% before FY26 second-half deleveraging.
inputs.last_fcf_note: AFFO proxy: FY26 FFO 892 less the Investment Management portfolio growth-capex line 'Payments for and development of investment properties' (211m, FY26 Annual Report cash flow statement line 6598) less plant/equipment/software (11m, line 6600) less land payments partially allocated (rounded to a combined ~7% of revenue in the projection, see capex_pct_path note). This is the FY0 anchor only; the projection charges capex at 7.0% of revenue in base.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Reported OCF-based FreeCashFlow (Metrics.csv, FY26: OCF 876 less capex_abs 222). Not the valuation flow: Stockland's OCF/FCF swings enormously year to year (-424 FY24 to +654 FY26) purely on MPC/LLC land-inventory working-capital timing (build vs settle), not on the underlying earnings power the FFO measure is designed to isolate. This is exactly the 'reported FCF can be structurally negative without distress' pattern SKILL.md flags for land subdividers/inventory-heavy developers, which is over half of Stockland's FFO.
inputs.sbc_source: No StockBasedComp column populated in Metrics.csv/core_metrics for SGP.AX. Security-based remuneration (LTI/STI rights) is expensed inside overheads that FFO already deducts (Stockland's FFO reconciliation starts from statutory profit and adds back only fair-value movements, non-cash items and one-off significant items -- not SBC). Charging it again in the engine would double-count; SBC path set to zero and the house/street band collapses (SBC-zero convention, same as GMG/SCG/CHC).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 finance income (13m, Annual Report line 6300) is netted inside FFO's net interest expense; no separate cash balance is added to EV, so there is nothing to strip out.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the flow (FFO) is already post-interest and post-tax. Built in AUD: 10-year ACGB ~4.3%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~0.95 (higher than a passive landlord REIT like SCG.AX (0.85, 8.5% CoE) or GPT.AX because over 60% of Stockland's FFO is tied to the cyclical residential/land-lease development cycle, which management itself flags is normalising down from an FY26 peak) => ~9.05%, used as 9.0%. One rate across scenarios; scenario risk is carried in the flows (growth, margin, capex, terminal cap), not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities are immaterial (31m total at FY26, note 8321, vs a $10.7bn equity base) and lease payments sit inside overheads/net interest that FFO already deducts. No separate charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Stockland reports no material non-controlling interest line in the consolidated statements; capital-partnering vehicles (M&G, Invesco, Mercer, Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing, EdgeConneX) are equity-accounted joint ventures/associates, not consolidated subsidiaries with minority interests, so Stockland's share of their FFO contribution is already the attributable measure with no NCI deduction needed.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine per SKILL.md's REIT row, despite Stockland being a diversified stapled group (Stockland Corporation Ltd share + Stockland Trust unit) with >60% of FFO development-derived rather than a pure passive landlord -- the same principle applies (FFO is a post-interest, post-tax distributable-earnings measure; statutory NPAT is materially inflated by non-cash investment-property revaluations, +202m in FY26) and the routing table's straddle guidance ('REIT with a big operating business... value the parts separately and sum') was considered but rejected: Stockland's own FFO measure already blends Investment Management and Development FFO into one number management uses for guidance and distribution policy, so splitting it into a component owner-FCF DCF for Development and a capitalisation model for Investment Management would require allocating shared corporate overheads and balance-sheet capital without a clean segment cash-flow disclosure to do so reliably; capitalising the single blended FFO stream is the more defensible read of the disclosed data. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue x 'ebitda_margin_path' = FFO (post-interest, post-tax); SBC, lease, D&A and cash-tax paths are zero because FFO already carries them; 'capex_pct_path' is the AFFO deduction, sized to the Investment Management portfolio's recurring growth capex (~5.9% of FY26 revenue: 'payments for and development of investment properties' 211m + plant/equipment/software 11m) plus a margin for net land-bank cash investment ahead of MPC/LLC margin realisation, giving ~7% of revenue in base; wacc field = cost of equity; net_debt = 0. FY26 ANCHOR: FFO 892m (+10.4%), FFO/security 36.9c (top end of 36.0-37.0c guidance), distribution 25.2 cps flat vs FY25 (69% payout, within the newly-recalibrated 60-80% target range, from a tighter historical band), gearing 22.7% (from 28.1% at H1 FY26 after 2H deleveraging), DRP suspended for 2H26. FY27 GUIDANCE: FFO/security 38.0-39.0c (management explicitly frames this as growth across Logistics/Retail/Data Centres/LLC/fee income more than offsetting a lower MPC contribution vs the FY26 settlement peak of 8,902 lots, guided down to 7,300-8,300 in FY27), distribution held flat at 25.2 cps. Base case year 1 (4.0% revenue growth, 25.0% FFO margin) lands at FFO/security 38.5c, the guidance midpoint. HISTORY: FFO margin has declined steadily from 29-32% (FY17-19) to 24.9% (FY26) as the revenue mix has shifted toward lower-margin MPC lot sales; FFO/security has grown only ~1.1%/yr over 9 years (33.4c FY17 to 36.9c FY26) despite 3.0%/yr revenue growth -- almost all top-line growth has been diluted by mix shift, which is why base-case terminal growth is capped at 2.5% rather than extrapolating the FY27 guided step-up. Model choice recorded for the memory line: first valuation of this ticker.

bear.narrative: FY2027 misses the bottom of guidance (36.0c) as the 2H FY26-flagged moderation in buyer sentiment (cumulative RBA tightening resumed Feb 2026, mortgage rates ~6.25-6.4%, Federal Budget tax-change uncertainty) deepens into an outright MPC/LLC settlement and pricing downturn for two years, and the Workplace portfolio's occupancy decline (91.1% to 86.6% in FY26) continues as change-of-use conversions slip. MPC development margin falls further below the guided ~20% toward the high teens as incentives rise back toward or above long-run averages. Cost of debt keeps climbing (already guided to ~5.9% in FY27 from 5.3%) as the fixed-hedge ratio (down to 65% from 76%) exposes more of the book to a higher-for-longer curve, and gearing drifts up from 22.7% toward the top of the 20-30% target band, raising the equity-funded capex share to 9% of revenue as capital-partnering appetite cools in a downturn. Terminal growth 1.5%, exit 12x FFO.

base.narrative: FY2027 lands at the guidance midpoint (revenue +4.0% at a 25.0% FFO margin, essentially flat vs FY26's 24.9%, gives FFO/security 38.5c against 38.0-39.0c guided). Growth then fades over three years as the guided MPC lot-volume step-down (7,300-8,300 vs FY26's 8,902) works through, before recovering to a 2.0% steady state as Logistics comparable growth (8.1% FY26), the Data Centres platform (first FY27 FFO contribution) and the scaling capital-partnering fee book (+20% FY26) mature into larger, more stable contributors. FFO margin drifts down slightly to 24.5% and holds, reflecting continued (but slowing) mix shift toward development revenue and the guided ~20% MPC margin (down from 21.2%). AFFO deduction 7.0% of revenue: the Investment Management portfolio's recurring growth capex (5.9% of FY26 revenue on the disclosed cash-flow-statement line) plus a margin for net land-bank cash investment ahead of MPC/LLC margin realisation. Terminal 17x FFO (below the Gordon value at 9.0%/2.5%, so the model is capped by the multiple, not the growth perpetuity).

bull.narrative: FY2027 beats the top of guidance (39.3c) as LLC settlements (guided 850-950, already raised vs FY26's 777) and Logistics releasing spreads (33.8% FY26) keep surprising, and the Data Centres platform (~450MW secured across three sites, further pipeline) begins monetising faster than the 'positive contribution' guided. New-build exemption from the 2027 negative-gearing changes supports MPC demand through the housing-policy transition rather than merely cushioning it. Fee income from the expanding capital-partnering platform (M&G, Invesco, Mercer, Morgan Stanley Real Estate Investing) keeps compounding at 20%+, lifting the blended FFO margin toward 27% as the group's capital intensity per dollar of FFO falls -- the AFFO capex charge falls to 5.5% of revenue as more growth is funded via co-investment rather than balance-sheet capital. Terminal growth 3.0%, exit 19x FFO.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 17x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 30/50/20 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 30%: over 60% of FFO is tied to the residential/land-lease development cycle, management's own FY27 guidance already embeds a lower MPC contribution than the FY26 peak, buyer sentiment was explicitly flagged as moderating through 2H FY26 on cumulative rate rises and tax-policy uncertainty, and the RBA resumed tightening in February 2026 -- this is a cyclical business entering a guided-down year, not a stable landlord. Bull cut to 20%: it requires the Data Centres platform, expanded capital partnerships and Logistics momentum to all outperform simultaneously while the MPC cycle does NOT deteriorate further, several distinct favourable outcomes stacking at once against a backdrop management itself describes as normalising from cyclical highs.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
